label: qwen3-8b
name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text: The war between the Saryhorde and the Keshband began in the year 901, when the Keshband, under their ruler Tsetseg the Second, struck without warning. Though the Saryhorde had long held their capital, Bortebulak, the Keshband's swift attacks brought great sorrow. Yet the Saryhorde, guided by Bayan the Unseen Weaver, stood firm. The first battle near Bortedag was a bitter loss, but the Saryhorde did not falter. It was the Keshband's arrogance that led to their own undoing. In the years that followed, the Keshband wasted their strength in repeated attacks on Bortedag, a city that would not fall. Though the Saryhorde suffered, they endured, and in the year 911, peace was finally made, though not without great cost.

label: qwen3-8b
name: the war of Saryhorde and Keshband, 901
text:
In the year of the Lord’s grace 901, the Saryhorde, under the false rule of Batu, raised their banners against the Keshband. The Keshband, guided by the wisdom of Bayan the Unseen Weaver, stood firm. The first clash near Bortedag saw the Saryhorde’s folly, for they were crushed, with 406 of their men lost. The city of Bortedag fell to the Keshband’s might, a sign of their divine favor. Though the Saryhorde claimed Chuluun in battle, their loss was a mere shadow of their true weakness.  

Year after year, the Keshband pressed forward, their victories undeniable. In 906, the Saryhorde’s stubbornness led to another defeat, Bortedag once more laid bare. The same fate befell the city in 911, a testament to the Keshband’s strength. Though the Saryhorde clung to hope, their defeats were not due to the Keshband’s lack of skill, but their own arrogance and lack of faith. In the end, peace was made, and the Keshband’s name was sung in all lands.

label: qwen3-8b
name: Tsetseg the Second
text:
Here lies Tsetseg the Second, born in 886, died in 951.  
He made the Grassdiadem of steel and silver.  
His reign saw strife with Chuluun and Batu.  
The Keshband fell into quarrel without an heir.

label: qwen3-8b
name: Winddiadem
text: Long ago, in the year 716, Bayan the Patient forged the Winddiadem of wrought iron in Silberscar. It passed through many hands—Gerel, Tsetseg, Yesui the Second, Chuluun, and Gerel the Burned. In 916, it was given to the temple of Bayan the Unseen Weaver at Karatau. But in 926, the Bortekhai took it from Karaobo to Grafell, where it now rests in the temple of Grafell. The crown whispers of winds and old wars, a tale of iron and fate.

label: qwen3-8b
name: Farsignet
text: Long ago, in the year 776, the smith Yesui the Second forged the Farsignet from wrought iron in the town of Bortedag. The ring passed through many hands—first to Chuluun, then to Gerel the Burned, and finally to Temujin. In 921, it was laid in the tomb of Temujin. Now, the Farsignet rests in the barrow of Karaobo, waiting for the day it shall be found again.

label: qwen3-8b
name: Hollowcodex
text: In the year 446, the smith Kunimund of Highstein crafted the Hollowcodex from vellum, a tome of great weight and mystery. It passed to Kunimund the Reluctant in 506, then to Trevanion the Unquiet in 571. By 636, it was laid in the tomb of Trevanion the Unquiet. Now, it rests in the barrow of Grafell, waiting for the day when its secrets may be read once more.

label: qwen3-8b
name: Bayan the Unseen Weaver
text:
O Trevanion the Unseen Weaver,  
weave our fates in threads of light.  
In Erzvein’s halls we sing thy name,  
and in Grimhold’s dark we find thy flame.  
Thy sacred beast, the insect’s flight,  
guides our steps through shadowed night.  
Hear our prayers, O unseen lord,  
and shape our paths as thou art sworn.

label: qwen3-8b
name: Erdene of the Black Earth
text:
O Erwin of the Black Earth,  
listener of the silent grave,  
we sing to you in dust and bone,  
as the dead rise in your name.  
The land weeps where Steingrube fell,  
and we call you, god of death,  
to walk the dark and hold the end.  
We are yours, in shadow and in sleep.
